html:
The Arhuaco, who call themselves Iku or Ijku, are an Indigenous people of the southern slopes of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in northern Colombia.

They are one of four peoples of the Sierra, with the Kogi, the Wiwa and the Kankuamo, who see themselves as descendants of the Tairona and as guardians of the mountain. Their spiritual leaders, the mamos, guide life in the community. Men wear white clothing and a white hat shaped like the snow peaks, and woven mochila bags are an important craft.

Capuchin missionaries ran a mission at Nabusímake, the Arhuaco centre, from 1916 until the Arhuaco expelled them in 1982. The Tairona town now called Ciudad Perdida lies in the Sierra.
sum: The Arhuaco, who call themselves Iku or Ijku, are an Indigenous people of the southern slopes of the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta in northern Colombia.
